enrichment.short_title: Inter-Tel v Ocis: harassment stay refused for lack of US enforceability
key_facts: Inter-Tel sued Ocis and its director for a course of harassing telephone calls linked to Arizona litigation.
Defendants applied to stay English proceedings on forum non conveniens grounds pointing to Arizona.
Arizona anti-harassment law was pleaded as an alternative basis for relief.
Claimants argued any US judgment would be unenforceable against foreign-domiciled defendants.
enrichment.procedural_posture: High Court application to stay harassment proceedings under CPR 11.
enrichment.outcome: Stay application dismissed; English proceedings to continue.
enrichment.ratio: Enforceability of any judgment is a legitimate and potentially decisive advantage for claimants; where Arizona would yield an empty judgment against foreign defendants, other connecting factors favouring Arizona do not make it clearly more appropriate than England.
legal_issues: Spiliada forum non conveniens test
Weight of enforceability under International Credit case
Whether Arizona courts could assume jurisdiction over foreign defendants
Application of English and Arizona harassment statutes
linked_authorities: Spiliada Maritime Corp v Cansulex Ltd [1987] AC 460
The International Credit Corporation v Morgan [1999] 1 WLR 1483

enrichment.short_title: Sandrasegarampillai: Sri Lankan asylum appeal dismissed on country conditions
key_facts: Sri Lankan appellant claimed asylum after alleged LTTE-related detentions and ill-treatment.
Adjudicator and IAT rejected the claim, finding improved security and no adverse interest on return.
Tribunal failed to refer to Jeyachandran and Selvaratnam authorities.
Court of Appeal reviewed whether the Tribunal's conclusion was an error of law.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal from Immigration Appeal Tribunal refusal of asylum appeal.
enrichment.ratio: Where country conditions have significantly improved and the appellant lacks a high profile, a tribunal may lawfully find no real risk of persecution or Article 3 ill-treatment on return despite past detentions, provided its reasoning adequately addresses the evidence.
legal_issues: Weight of improved country conditions in Sri Lanka
Effect of prior army detentions and alleged brutality
Tribunal duty to consider relevant IAT and Court of Appeal authorities
Article 3 threshold on return
linked_authorities: Selvaratnam v Secretary of State [2003] EWCA Civ 121
Jeyachandran v Secretary of State [2002] UKIAT 01869

enrichment.short_title: Fidler v Reigate: planning enforcement and material change of use
key_facts: Mr Fidler used Honeycrock Farmyard for commercial activities contrary to agricultural planning unit status.
Reigate and Banstead served enforcement notices requiring cessation of business uses.
Inspector allowed part of the appeal but the council challenged material change of use and deemed permission issues.
House of Lords decision in Scott was central to time limits for enforcement.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Court of Appeal from planning inquiry decision on enforcement notices.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal dismissed; matter remitted for reconsideration in light of Scott and the court's judgment.
enrichment.ratio: Following Scott, planning authorities need not identify every continuing breach before enforcement action; the appellant's construction would impose an unreasonable burden on authorities; enforcement notice appeals turn on material change of use and lawful planning history.
legal_issues: Meaning of material change of use within planning unit C
Application of Scott to enforcement time limits
Deemed planning permission issue
Scope of remittal to inspector

enrichment.short_title: Omnibridge v Clearsprings: bonus clause construction in arbitration award
key_facts: OCL claimed a bonus under a consultancy agreement with CML after a government compensation payment.
An arbitrator made an interim award on clause 4.11 bonus entitlement.
CML alleged an oral collateral condition precedent; OCL challenged parts of the award under sections 68 and 69.
CML cross-applied under section 68 and sought extension of time.
enrichment.procedural_posture: High Court applications under sections 68 and 69 arising from an interim arbitration award.
enrichment.outcome: Partial remission ordered on rate-related passages; CML section 68 application dismissed; further argument on order form.
enrichment.ratio: Clause 4.11 is construed on its ordinary wording without importing an alleged uncorroborated oral collateral agreement; section 68/69 challenges may be limited to specific irregularities warranting remission rather than setting aside the whole award.
legal_issues: Construction of bonus clause 4.11
Oral collateral contract and condition precedent
Scope of section 68 serious irregularity
Partial remission versus setting aside interim award

enrichment.short_title: Newham v GLMCA: magistrates wrongly refused to issue all summonses
key_facts: Newham laid informations seeking multiple summonses against a landlord for housing offences.
Stratford magistrates issued only a reduced number of summonses exercising discretion.
Council challenged the refusal as unlawful fettering of prosecution informations.
Davis J considered whether magistrates could limit process where informations were properly laid.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Judicial review of magistrates' court decision refusing to issue summonses.
enrichment.outcome: Claim upheld; declaratory relief granted that refusal was flawed; no order as to costs.
enrichment.ratio: Magistrates have discretion whether to issue summons on informations laid, but it is not unfettered; refusing to issue process in the form properly requested may be unlawful where it frustrates prosecution within time limits.
legal_issues: Scope of magistrates' discretion on issuing summonses
Duty when informations properly laid by local authority
Declaratory relief in magistrates' court JR
Costs in JR against magistrates' authority

enrichment.short_title: McCubbin: assault case stated appeal dismissed as disguised fact challenge
key_facts: Mr McCubbin was convicted of assault in Sutton magistrates' court and conditionally discharged.
He appealed by case stated rather than to the Crown Court.
Administrative Court considered whether magistrates erred in law on self-defence/provocation.
Prosecution argued the appeal challenged findings of fact dressed as error of law.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal by way of case stated from magistrates' assault conviction.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal dismissed; case stated question answered in the affirmative; costs £800.
enrichment.ratio: The Administrative Court must guard against appeals that are in truth challenges to magistrates' findings of fact; Crown Court appeal with rehearing is the appropriate route where factual dispute exists.
legal_issues: Limits of case stated appeal versus Crown Court appeal
Whether magistrates' assault findings involved error of law
Costs on dismissed case stated appeal

enrichment.short_title: R v Lomey: absolute discharge refused on Attorney General reference
key_facts: Lomey received life and concurrent terms in 1984 for GBH with intent and aggravated burglaries.
After long period at liberty on life licence he sought absolute discharge via Attorney General reference.
Medical evidence showed he no longer required hospital detention.
Court considered whether to substitute absolute discharge to remove life licence stigma.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Court of Appeal on reference/resentence of historic indeterminate sentence.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal/reference dismissed; absolute discharge refused despite sympathy.
enrichment.ratio: The Court lacks power to order Mental Health Act disposal where no current mental disorder warrants detention; minimal recall risk does not justify absolute discharge for grave historic offences meriting life sentence.
legal_issues: Power to impose absolute discharge on reference
Interaction of life licence and mental health disposal
Whether stigma of life licence justifies discharge after long liberty

enrichment.short_title: Stephenson v Stockton: community care charges and family member rule

statutes_considered.title: Health and Social Services and Social Security Adjudications Act 1983

key_facts: Elderly sheltered housing tenant challenged Stockton's community care charges.
Council applied a family member rule limiting non-resident family contributions to care costs.
Claimant argued policy unlawfully excluded other exceptional cases.
Council framework document did not fully spell out exceptions policy.
enrichment.procedural_posture: High Court judicial review of local authority community care charging policy.
enrichment.outcome: Claim dismissed; parties to agree costs with possible reduction for unclear framework document.
enrichment.ratio: A local authority may lawfully apply a family member rule in charging assessments where framework permits exceptions including cultural cases; failure to spell out exceptions in the framework document may affect costs but not necessarily vitiate the decision.
